paragraphs.text: This chapter drops you straight into Hamburg, Germany's big northern port on the river Elbe. There is no story to follow here — you read the city instead: short caption texts full of names and numbers, the kind printed under a photo in a travel guide.

That format is also the first skill of this lesson. A German text about a place rarely hides its facts. If you recognise a handful of nouns and can pick the numbers out around them, you already understand more than you expect. The concert hall on the second photo is the {{de:Elbphilharmonie}} — a good first test: how much can you read before anyone translates anything?
Willkommen in Hamburg! Hamburg ist groß. Der Hafen ist bekannt, die Elbphilharmonie ist neu, und jeden Tag fahren hier Hunderte von Zügen.

items.german: Der Hauptbahnhof: In 8 Stunden nach Warschau, in 6 Stunden nach München, in 5 Stunden nach Kopenhagen, in 2 Stunden nach Berlin. Jeden Tag fahren hier 720 Züge.
items.english: The main train station: 8 hours to Warsaw, 6 hours to Munich, 5 hours to Copenhagen, 2 hours to Berlin. Every day 720 trains go from here.

items.german: Die Elbphilharmonie ist der Star in Hamburg. Bauzeit: 9 Jahre (2007 bis 2016). Kosten: 866 Millionen Euro. Im ersten Jahr (2017) 4,5 Millionen Besucher und 600 Konzerte.
items.english: The Elbphilharmonie is Hamburg's star. Construction: 9 years (2007 to 2016). Cost: 866 million euro. In its first year (2017), 4.5 million visitors and 600 concerts.
